output.summary: The shrink increase is mainly a receiving-control failure. Removing backdoor receiving clerks in April 2025 left DSD deliveries unverified. DSD categories account for 73% of the increase. Shrink rose to 3.0% in the 41 no-clerk stores versus 1.7% in the 17 clerk stores. The audit found invoices exceeding counted value by 4.9%. A matched-control pilot cut DSD shrink from 4.4% to 1.9%. District 4's bag-check and discipline policy found almost nothing and suppressed shortage claims, so it should not be extended. POS exceptions and associate-theft cases were flat, count-firm validation showed no inflation, and cameras showed no effect. Organized crime in the urban stores is plausible but unquantified and confounded. Locked cases lose more margin than they save. Reinstate count-before-sign-off receiving first.
